tier_reason: The independent krausest suite (implementation in frameworks/non-keyed/delorean) has the numbers, and my medians from results.ts reproduce the record exactly, but the headline win compares a NON-KEYED implementation with keyed React hooks, a mode the suite's README says can avoid costly DOM operations. Against the like-for-like JS baseline, vanillajs-non-keyed, the geometric mean is 1.010x (not faster). Asymmetric-baseline precedent (GStreamer B to C), so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README bullet: 'Fastest than vanillajs', linking to the suite site; the suite does not support it. Suite data, my unweighted geometric means over the 9 CPU benchmarks of median total duration from the raw run arrays in results.ts (derived from page data): versus vanillajs-non-keyed 1.010x the time (not faster); versus vanillajs-3-non-keyed 1.112x (slower); versus svelte-classic-v5.13.0-non-keyed 0.885x. Rank 7 of 67 non-keyed implementations by slowdown versus the per-benchmark best (1.138), behind vanillajs-3, mikado, deleight, solarite, vanillajs-1 and vanillajs non-keyed. Cross-mode (non-keyed versus keyed, not like-for-like): 0.522x the time of react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed (0.649x excluding swap rows) and 0.951x vanillajs-keyed. Swap 1,000 rows 8.2 ms vs React 89.7 ms; create 1,000 rows 22.9 ms vs 23.6 ms; create 10,000 rows 237.4 ms vs 401.0 ms.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust release profile lto=true, panic=abort (opt-level left at the default); wasm-pack through @wasm-tool/wasm-pack-plugin 0.4.2 with webpack 4.33.0 (frameworks/non-keyed/delorean). The benchmark Cargo.toml depends on the crates.io delorean 0.2.1 (published 2020-10-06), although the suite labels the entry v0.1.0 and the latest crate is 0.3.0 (2023-03-30). The bundled-dist is checked in prebuilt; the rustc and wasm-bindgen versions that built it are not stated.
corrections.hardware: Apple M4 (MacBook Pro 14, '14/20 cores', 48 GB RAM), macOS 26.6.2, Chrome 154.0.8037.98 (arm64), per the 'Test environment & methodology' block in webdriver-ts-results/src/App.tsx, which ships with the Chrome 154 results (results.ts commit c097071 'Chrome 154 results', 2026-10-04). The same page sets isOfficial = false and labels itself a development snapshot that 'may mix browser versions or run counts'.
corrections.workload: krausest/js-framework-benchmark: nine browser benchmarks on a 1,000/10,000-row table (create, replace all, partial update, select, swap, remove, create 10k, append, clear), driven by the Puppeteer benchmark driver with reduced tracing (15 runs per benchmark, 25 for select), median of the total (script plus paint) duration per benchmark.
corrections.caveats: Non-keyed implementation: the suite's README says non-keyed mode 'can be more performant, since costly DOM operations can be avoided', so the win over keyed React hooks (largest on swap rows, 8.2 vs 89.7 ms, and replace all, 0.42x) is partly a mode difference. The suite has no non-keyed React entry. Against non-keyed vanilla JS the entry is not faster (1.010x vanillajs-non-keyed, 1.112x vanillajs-3-non-keyed), so the README's 'Fastest than vanillajs' is unsupported. The benchmark code hand-writes the App trait's __render and __hydrate methods with direct web-sys DOM calls and dirty bitmasks (src/app.rs, src/row.rs), in effect manual DOM manipulation, although the suite flags it only with note 1139 ('Implementation doesn't pass strict CSP') and not with note 772; delorean itself is described on crates.io as 'A simple single thread reactor pattern for wasm', so the measured speed is mostly that of the hand-written DOM code. The prebuilt bundle was built against delorean 0.2.1 (2020) while the suite labels it v0.1.0. results.ts is shipped with a page marked as a development snapshot (isOfficial = false). Ratios are my own unweighted geometric means from the raw results.ts, not the site's weighted score. Repo last commit 2023-03-30, 4 stars; the crates.io record points at github.com/botika/delorean, apparently the same author's earlier account name.

notes: Real third-party numbers, verified exactly, but the React comparison is non-keyed versus keyed and the like-for-like vanilla JS non-keyed baseline is as fast or faster (1.010x, 1.112x). The measured code is hand-written web-sys DOM manipulation, so little of the speed is attributable to the delorean crate. Shortcomings: cross-mode baseline, not faster than vanilla JS, manual DOM code, stale prebuilt bundle from a 2020 crate version, abandoned repo with 4 stars.

tier_reason: Well-known independent suite (implementation in frameworks/keyed/dioxus, driver in webdriver-ts), and my medians from results.ts reproduce the record exactly. The run's CPU (Apple M4) and Chrome build are stated in webdriver-ts-results/src/App.tsx and the Cargo.toml flags are public. It stays B, not A, because the checked-in prebuilt bundle names no rustc, trunk or wasm-bindgen version and the results page is flagged as a development snapshot.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README claims are about size ('Simple "hello world" at about 50kb, comparable to React', 'Build WebApps weighing less than 50kb'); it gives no rendering-speed number. Suite data, my unweighted geometric means over the 9 CPU benchmarks of median total duration from the raw run arrays in results.ts (derived from page data): 0.698x the time of react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed (about 1.43x faster; 0.838x excluding swap rows); 0.715x preact-hooks; 1.002x vue-v3.5.39-keyed; 1.272x vanillajs-keyed; 1.151x solid-v1.9.3-keyed; 1.073x svelte-v5.42.1-keyed. Swap 1,000 rows 14.6 ms vs React 89.7 ms; create 1,000 rows 24.1 ms vs 23.6 ms; create 10,000 rows 257.9 ms vs 401.0 ms. Rank 90 of 196 keyed implementations by slowdown versus the per-benchmark best (1.331).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: dioxus 0.7.2 with dioxus-web 0.7.2 (default-features = false); Rust release profile opt-level=3, lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort, strip=true, incremental=false; trunk build --release (frameworks/keyed/dioxus/Cargo.toml, build.sh, trunk.toml). The bundled-dist is checked in prebuilt; the rustc, trunk and wasm-bindgen versions that built it are not stated.
corrections.hardware: Apple M4 (MacBook Pro 14, '14/20 cores', 48 GB RAM), macOS 26.6.2, Chrome 154.0.8037.98 (arm64), per the 'Test environment & methodology' block in webdriver-ts-results/src/App.tsx, which ships with the Chrome 154 results (results.ts commit c097071 'Chrome 154 results', 2026-10-04). The same page sets isOfficial = false and labels itself a development snapshot that 'may mix browser versions or run counts'.
corrections.workload: krausest/js-framework-benchmark: nine browser benchmarks on a 1,000/10,000-row table (create, replace all, partial update, select, swap, remove, create 10k, append, clear), driven by the Puppeteer benchmark driver with reduced tracing (15 runs per benchmark, 25 for select), median of the total (script plus paint) duration per benchmark.
corrections.caveats: Independent public suite with the CPU (Apple M4) and Chrome 154.0.8037.98 stated, but the toolchain versions behind the checked-in prebuilt bundle are not stated ('build-prod' is a no-op: 'the generated javascript is already provided'), so the shipped binary may not match the source, and the results page is marked a development snapshot (isOfficial = false). The win over React hooks is largest on swap rows (89.7 vs 14.6 ms, React hooks' known weak spot); without swap it is 0.838x React's time, and create 1,000 rows is 1.02x React's time. Not faster than the best JavaScript entries (1.272x vanillajs-keyed, 1.151x Solid, 1.073x Svelte, level with Vue 3.5); slowdown versus the per-benchmark best is 1.54 across all implementations, against vanillajs keyed 1.21, Solid keyed 1.34 and Svelte keyed 1.44 (derived from page data). Flagged by suite note 1139 ('Implementation doesn't pass strict CSP'). Bundle sizes are larger than React's in the same results (compressed 114.9 kB vs 51.4 kB; first paint 540.9 vs 226.6 ms). Ratios are my own unweighted geometric means from the raw results.ts, not the site's weighted score.

notes: Numbers verified exactly from the raw run arrays; React hooks is a fair keyed JS baseline and Dioxus beats it on 7 of 9 benchmarks, but it is level with Vue and slower than vanilla JS, Solid and Svelte. Hardware found in the results app's App.tsx (MacBook Pro 14, Apple M4, macOS 26.6.2, Chrome 154.0.8037.98 arm64). Tier B rather than A only because the prebuilt bundle's toolchain is unstated and the results page is a development snapshot. Metadata matches: 39.4k stars, MIT or Apache-2.0, last commit 2026-10-09.

tier_reason: Well-known independent suite (implementation in frameworks/keyed/elementaryui) with a keyed React hooks row, and my medians from results.ts reproduce the record exactly. The CPU (Apple M4) and Chrome build are stated in webdriver-ts-results/src/App.tsx, but no swiftc version or optimisation flags are, the bundle is prebuilt and the page is a development snapshot, so B, not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Project makes no speed claim; README claims only size ('Full Embedded Swift support means kB-sized wasm bundles instead of MB'). Suite data, my unweighted geometric means over the 9 CPU benchmarks of median total duration from the raw run arrays in results.ts (derived from page data): 0.877x the time of react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed (about 1.14x faster), but 1.081x React's time (slower) when swap rows is excluded; 0.898x preact-hooks; 1.258x vue-v3.5.39-keyed; 1.597x vanillajs-keyed; 1.446x solid-v1.9.3-keyed; 1.348x svelte-v5.42.1-keyed. Per benchmark versus React: swap 14.7 vs 89.7 ms, create 10,000 rows 349.6 vs 401.0 ms and clear faster (0.91x); create 1,000 rows 31.9 vs 23.6 ms (1.35x), replace all 1.22x, append 1.30x, partial update 1.03x and select 1.06x slower; remove level. Rank 136 of 196 keyed implementations by slowdown versus the per-benchmark best (1.671 keyed-only, 1.937 across all).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Embedded Swift: vite.config.js calls swiftWasm({ useEmbeddedSDK: true, linkEmbeddedUnicodeDataTables: false }) from @elementary-swift/vite-plugin-swift-wasm 0.2.0 with vite 8.3.1; Package.swift pins elementary-ui exact 0.8.0 and JavaScriptKit from 0.58.0 (swift-tools-version 6.3, Swift 5 language mode). The swiftc toolchain version and optimisation flags are not stated; bundled-dist is checked in prebuilt.
corrections.hardware: Apple M4 (MacBook Pro 14, '14/20 cores', 48 GB RAM), macOS 26.6.2, Chrome 154.0.8037.98 (arm64), per the 'Test environment & methodology' block in webdriver-ts-results/src/App.tsx, which ships with the Chrome 154 results (results.ts commit c097071 'Chrome 154 results', 2026-10-04). The same page sets isOfficial = false and labels itself a development snapshot that 'may mix browser versions or run counts'.
corrections.workload: krausest/js-framework-benchmark: nine browser benchmarks on a 1,000/10,000-row table (create, replace all, partial update, select, swap, remove, create 10k, append, clear), driven by the Puppeteer benchmark driver with reduced tracing (15 runs per benchmark, 25 for select), median of the total (script plus paint) duration per benchmark.
corrections.caveats: Independent suite with the CPU (Apple M4) and Chrome 154.0.8037.98 stated, but the swiftc toolchain and flags behind the checked-in prebuilt bundle are not, and the results page is marked a development snapshot (isOfficial = false). The 1.14x geometric-mean win over React hooks comes entirely from swap rows (React hooks' known weak spot, 89.7 vs 14.7 ms): without it ElementaryUI is 1.081x React's time, and it is slower than React on 5 of 9 benchmarks (create 1,000 rows 1.35x, append 1.30x, replace all 1.22x). It is 1.6x slower than vanilla JS (the category's JS-in-V8 baseline) and slower than Vue, Solid and Svelte. Flagged by suite note 1139 ('Implementation doesn't pass strict CSP'). Bundle size and first paint are larger than React's (compressed 143.7 kB vs 51.4 kB; first paint 815.9 vs 226.6 ms). Ratios are my own unweighted geometric means from the raw results.ts, not the site's weighted score.

notes: Numbers verified exactly from the raw arrays. The 'faster than React' result rests on one benchmark (swap rows); excluding it the entry is 1.08x slower than React, and it is 1.6x slower than vanilla JS. Record the shortcoming 'faster than React hooks only on swap, create 10k and clear; slower on 5 of 9; not faster than the JS baseline'. The benchmark build uses the Embedded Swift SDK (useEmbeddedSDK: true), which the record left unstated. Metadata matches: 511 stars, Apache-2.0, last commit 2026-10-09.
